kept.title: Bulk frame and stream bounds of §16 are not the ones the code enforces, and protocol/limits.go's bulk constants are dead
kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: §8.1 'trames u32 length … length ≤ 1 065 005'; §16.1 rows 'trame vrac 1 065 005 o | violation' and 'flux par pair et par sens … vrac 1 | violation'; §16 'Les bornes sont des constantes exportées de protocol ; un test par ligne vérifie la borne'
kept.evidence: bulk.go:164 reads up to transport.MaxFrame (protocol/peer.go:29 'MaxFrame = 64<<20 - 3 - maxPeerIDLen'); bulk.go:24-26 'maxBulkStreams = 4' used at node.go:498-502 for Streams/Inbound/Outbound; protocol/limits.go:30 'BulkStreams = 1', :36 'MaxBulkFrame = 1065005', :125-150 BulkRequestsPerPeer, BulkIdleTimeout, BulkRangeFailures, BulkConsecutiveBusy, BulkServesPerPeer, BulkMinGlobalServes, BulkBusyPerMinute, BulkFaultsBeforeBan, BulkBanDuration, ConcurrentBlobTransfers: grep finds no use outside limits.go; protocol/limits_test.go:28-93 only compares limits.go to testdata/limits.json, never to the implementation.
kept.scenario: A member sends bulk frames of 1 065 006 to ~64 MiB. Each one is read and allocated in full, then refused by blob.Decode and counted only as a 'fault' (see the violation finding), not as a violation at the header. A peer may also keep 4 bulk streams per direction instead of 1. Every bound test passes because nothing ties the exported constants to the code.
kept.fix: Use protocol.MaxBulkFrame and protocol.BulkStreams (+1 while closing, written into the spec) in p2p. Replace each private constant in internal/blob/service.go with the protocol constant. Add one test per §16 bulk row that drives the real lane at the bound and at bound + 1.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed but mostly a duplicate. The bulk constants at limits.go:30, :36 and :125-150 (BulkStreams, MaxBulkFrame, BulkRequestsPerPeer ... ConcurrentBlobTransfers) are used in no Go file other than limits.go. maxBulkStreams = 4 (bulk.go:26) feeds the resource manager (node.go:498-502), while §16.1 says vrac 1. The exploitable part, reading frames up to MaxFrame (bulk.go:164), is N-6 and finding 0. What remains is dead constants and a 4-versus-1 stream bound, so minor.

The frame-size part duplicates N-6 (inventaire.md:69). What is new holds up: maxBulkStreams = 4 (bulk.go:24-26), used at node.go:498-502, while spec §16.1 says 'vrac 1' per peer and direction with no closing allowance (unlike repo '+1 en fermeture'). Also, rtk proxy grep shows that MaxBulkFrame, BulkStreams, BulkBusyPerMinute and ConcurrentBlobTransfers appear only in protocol/limits.go. Nothing ties the exported §16 constants to the enforcing code, although §16 says 'un test par ligne vérifie la borne'. Lowered to minor because the only harm beyond N-6 is extra streams, which the resource manager still bounds.

kept.title: Bulk stream accepted from a non-member during the invitation window
kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: §12 step 1 'qui : clé valide ; membre, ou fenêtre d'invitation pour le salon seul'
kept.evidence: bulk.go:139-147 'if !n.admitted(p) { return }' then waitUp; node.go:530-538 admitted returns true when n.isOpen(); stream.go:47-58 onConnected marks ps.admitted from the same predicate, and stream.go:110-116 openOut sets ps.up = true, so waitUp (stream.go:284-302) succeeds for the stranger.
kept.scenario: While an admin's invitation window is open, any authenticated stranger connects. Its bulk frames are read and queued to blob.Service: a stall as in the critical finding, malformed frames up to 64 MiB, or a flood of unsolicited SLICEs. The window should allow it the lobby only.
kept.fix: Bulk.handle (and Send) must require Options.Admit(name), meaning a member; better, the active-member predicate. Never accept a stream because of isOpen(). Add a test: a stranger admitted by the window gets its bulk stream reset.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. bulk.go:139-141 accepts any peer with n.admitted(p). node.go:538 returns true while isOpen() holds, so a stranger gets in during the invitation window. stream.go:47-58 marks the stranger admitted, and stream.go:108-116 openOut sets ps.up, so waitUp (stream.go:284-302) succeeds and its frames are read and queued (bulk.go:162-178). The spec §12 step 1 limits the window to the lobby only. blob.Service gates only WANTs, through Allowed (service.go:221), so the stall of finding 0 and floods of unsolicited frames are open to strangers. None of the excluded reviews covers this (the admission-invite review is about Ask, flow.go).

Confirmed. bulk.go:139-147 checks only n.admitted(p). node.go:530-538 returns true while isOpen(). stream.go:47-58 sets ps.admitted, and openOut sets ps.up = true (stream.go:110-116), so waitUp succeeds and the stranger's bulk frames are read and queued. blob.Service only refuses its WANTs (service.go:221-224); a SLICE still goes through Decode/deliver, and the N-6 stall works. Spec §12 step 1 limits the invitation window to the lobby. Not in the IV1 review (ultrareview-admission-invite.md covers flow.go and the Ask lifetime only). Reachable by the invitee, an unattested peer, who must be strictly bounded.

kept.title: Requester sends more than 2 requests at a time to one peer; server answers BUSY instead of treating it as a violation
kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: §8.1 'Au plus une demande en cours par (pair, hash) et au plus 2 par pair … Demander plus de 2 à la fois est une violation.'; §16.1 'vrac (demandeur) 1 demande par (pair, hash), 2 par pair'
kept.evidence: service.go:24 'MaxTransfers = 4' and :471-475 one slot per download; :397-414 pick sorts the same best peer first for every download; :348-357 open only enforces one per (peer, hash); no per-peer count anywhere on the requester side. Server: service.go:228-237 a third concurrent WANT, or a second for the same hash, gets 'reply = Busy{…}' with no fault or violation; test service_test.go:886-890 sends 20 WANTs for the same hash and expects only BUSY.
kept.scenario: Four blobs are fetched at once from a project with one holder. Go sends 4 concurrent WANTs to that peer, so an honest inkwell requester breaks the spec bound, and a conformant third-party server would close its connection as a violation. A Go server never punishes a peer that keeps 20 WANTs outstanding: it only answers BUSY.
kept.fix: Add a per-peer outstanding counter (protocol.BulkRequestsPerPeer) in Service.open, and make pick skip saturated peers. On the server, make a 2nd WANT for the same (peer, hash) or a 3rd overall a violation (or change the spec to BUSY, but not both behaviours). Add vectors and tests for both sides.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. MaxTransfers = 4 (service.go:24) downloads run at once. Each pull takes peers[0] from pick (service.go:397-414), which sorts identically for every download. open (service.go:348-358) refuses only a second request per (peer, hash), and the requester keeps no per-peer count, so one holder can receive 4 concurrent WANTs, above the spec's 2. On the server side, a WANT beyond servingBy[peer] < maxServingPerPeer goes to the Busy branch (service.go:228-237) and is never treated as a violation.

The requester side is confirmed. MaxTransfers = 4 slots (service.go:24, :471-475). pick sorts the same best peer first for every download (:397-414). open only forbids a second request per (peer, hash) (:348-357), and nothing counts requests per peer. So a single holder receives 4 concurrent WANTs, against §8.1 'au plus 2 par pair … Demander plus de 2 à la fois est une violation'. The server side is weaker than claimed: §16.1's server row gives 'BUSY, puis silence' as the behaviour at the bound, so answering BUSY (service.go:228-237) matches that row, and the spec contradicts itself there. Kept for the requester breaking a MUST that a conformant server may treat as a violation.

kept.title: Serving capacity fixed at 8 with no reserved share per peer; the 32-BUSY bound is global, not per peer per minute
kept.question: hostile-peer
kept.rule: §8.1 'Chaque pair actif a une part réservée d'au moins une demande servie à la fois (§10.6), deux au plus'; '… un serveur envoie au plus 32 BUSY par pair et par minute'; §16.1 'vrac (serveur) 2 par pair ; max(8, 2n) au total ; 32 BUSY par pair et par minute | ≥ 1 par pair'
kept.evidence: service.go:30 'defaultMaxServing = 8', :131-132 cmp.Or default, app/files.go:149-155 passes no MaxServing; service.go:42-43 'maxBusyReplies = 32' is a global count of in-flight BUSY sends (:231-245 v.busy++ … v.busy--), with no per-peer or per-minute accounting; a serve holds its slot through v.send → Bulk.Send (bulk.go:210-220), which waits on the per-peer bulkSem and then WriteProgress(writeTimeout=90 s, FloorRate 2 KiB/s) (frame/progress.go:53: idle + len/FloorRate ≈ 90 s + 520 s for a full slice).
kept.scenario: Four colluding members, or four devices of one Byzantine person, each send 2 WANTs and read their stream at a trickle (one 32 KiB chunk every <90 s). Each holds 2 serving slots for up to ~10 min, renewable, so all 8 slots are taken. Each also queues up to 32 BUSY replies behind its own bulkSem, which uses up the global BUSY budget. Every honest member's WANT then gets silence (service.go:234-236) and fails after 30 s. TestServingIsFairBetweenPeers (service_test.go:863-929) proves fairness for 2 peers only.
kept.fix: Set the total to max(protocol.BulkMinGlobalServes, 2·n active peers). Reserve one slot per active peer, taken before the shared pool. Count BUSY per peer per minute (protocol.BulkBusyPerMinute). Add a test with k greedy drip-reading peers and one modest peer that must be served within one slice time.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. MaxServing defaults to a fixed 8 (service.go:30, :132), and files.go:149-155 passes no MaxServing, so max(8, 2n) is absent. maxBusyReplies (service.go:43) counts BUSY sends in flight across all peers (v.busy++/-- at :231-245), with no per-peer or per-minute accounting. A serve holds its slot through v.send → Bulk.Send, which waits on the per-peer bulkSem (bulk.go:210-214) and then WriteProgress, whose budget is idle + len/FloorRate (progress.go:53, FloorRate = 2 KiB/s at :29). So BUSY replies to a slow peer pile up behind its bulkSem and use up the global 32, and four slow members fill all 8 slots. Beyond 32, a WANT gets silence (service.go:234-236). The spec's reserved share of at least 1 per peer is not enforced.

Confirmed. defaultMaxServing = 8 is fixed (service.go:30, :131-132) instead of max(8, 2n), with maxServingPerPeer = 2 (:40-41), so 4 hostile members (readers included, since Allowed admits active members) take every slot. A serve holds its slot through v.send → Bulk.Send, which waits on bulkSem with the Run ctx and no deadline (bulk.go:210-214), and then WriteProgress (writeTimeout = frame.WriteIdle, FloorRate 2 KiB/s; progress.go:53). maxBusyReplies = 32 is a global count of in-flight BUSY sends (service.go:42-43, :231-245) with no per-peer or per-minute accounting. A single slow peer can queue 32 BUSY sends behind its own bulkSem, after which an honest peer gets silence (:234-236). Spec §16.1 asks for a share ≥ 1 per peer.

kept.title: A SLICE that does not carry the requested offset and length is accepted, and short answers stall the request with no fault
kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: §8.1 'un SLICE DOIT reprendre l'offset demandé et la length demandée, sauf pour la plage qui contient la fin du blob, où length = taille − offset'
kept.evidence: service.go:597-606 a verdict 'stored' keeps waiting; :626-640 accept stores any slice that verifies ('judged on what it says it is'), whatever its Offset/Length; :636 complete only if d.covers(offset, length); :737-757 checkSlice accepts any group-aligned length; pending.next (:380-391) keeps the deadline set at send (:373), so a short answer leaves the request waiting until that 30 s deadline; :584 v.answered(peer) clears strikes on every message.
kept.scenario: A hostile holder answers each 1 MiB WANT with a valid 16 KiB slice at the requested offset. It is stored, the exchange waits out the 30 s deadline, and the attempt fails with only a strike, which the next answer clears again. Without another holder the download runs at 16 KiB per 30 s, the peer is never faulted, and Fetch ends with ErrNoPeer after 8 attempts. Any late slice at any offset is also fully Bao-decoded (≤ 1 MiB of CPU and allocation) instead of being judged against the outstanding request.
kept.fix: Match the slice to the outstanding request: offset equal, and length equal or equal to size − offset at the end. Anything else is a fault (or explicitly a 'late answer to a cancelled request' with the 60 s rule). Add a bulk+expect vector with an outstanding {offset,length} and a mismatching SLICE.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed but the impact is small. accept (service.go:626-640) stores any slice that checkSlice verifies, without comparing m.Offset/m.Length to the request, and a 'stored' verdict keeps waiting until the deadline set at send (service.go:373, :380-391). answered (service.go:584) clears strikes on every reply. This departs from the spec's 'un SLICE DOIT reprendre l'offset demandé et la length demandée'. Lowered to minor: tried[peer]++ (service.go:547) moves the next attempt to other holders, and a sole holder can already deny the blob by staying silent. Bao decoding happens only while a request for that (peer, hash) is outstanding (deliver, service.go:267-274).

The divergence is real. accept (service.go:626-640) stores any slice that verifies whatever its Offset/Length, completes only if d.covers (:636), and otherwise returns 'stored' and keeps waiting until the deadline set at send (:373, :380-391). answered (:584) clears strikes on every message, and nothing faults a slice that does not echo the requested offset/length (§8.1 'DOIT reprendre'). Impact is lower than claimed. A sole hostile holder can deny the blob by silence anyway. With an honest holder, the timeout's strike (:584 then strike) sorts the hostile peer after peers with 0 strikes in pick (:405-408), so it costs about one 30 s stall per range.

kept.title: Size announced by bao checked after allocation and full Bao decoding
kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: §8.1 'Avant toute allocation, le demandeur vérifie que la taille totale annoncée par bao égale la taille attendue (index du projet) et que offset < taille ; sinon faute (#slice-size-mismatch)'
kept.evidence: service.go:627 checkSlice runs first: :747 reads the size, :759 'buf := bytes.NewBuffer(make([]byte, 0, int(n)))' allocates up to 1 MiB, :760 runs bao.DecodeSlice over the whole slice; only then :632 'if size == uint64(d.size)'. Vector slice-size-mismatch is 'proposed', enforce step-5 (bulk.json); decoder 'bulk+expect' is absent from conformance/reference.go:31-49 decoderTable.
kept.scenario: A peer answers with slices whose bao header gives the wrong total size. Each one costs a 1 MiB allocation and a full BLAKE3/Bao pass before the mismatch is seen. The rule the spec states as cheap and first is the last check applied.
kept.fix: Compare binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(m.Bao[:8]) with d.size and m.Offset < d.size in accept, before checkSlice allocates. Implement the 'bulk+expect' decoder in protocol/conformance so slice-size-mismatch is enforced.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed ordering. checkSlice reads the size at service.go:747, allocates bytes.NewBuffer(make(..., n)) at :759 (n ≤ MaxSlice) and runs bao.DecodeSlice at :760. Only after that does accept compare the size with d.size (:632). The spec asks for this check before any allocation. Minor: the frame was already allocated by the transport, the cost is at most 1 MiB and one Bao pass per solicited slice, and that cost is limited by flow control.

Confirmed ordering. checkSlice reads the size (:747), allocates up to n (:759) and runs bao.DecodeSlice (:760) before accept compares size with d.size (:632). §8.1 requires that comparison 'avant toute allocation'. The slice-size-mismatch vector is proposed/step-5 with decoder bulk+expect, which is absent from decoderTable (reference.go:31-49). Minor: the extra cost (≤ 1 MiB allocation and one hash pass) is bounded by bytes the peer has already sent and only applies to an open (peer, hash) request.

kept.title: Size-mismatch handling in code (confirmSize sub-exchange, no fault, discard on final) is not what the spec says
kept.question: code-to-spec
kept.rule: §8.1 'sinon faute (#slice-size-mismatch)'; §8.1 'Une faute (Bao invalide, taille fausse …) compte contre le pair'; §13 row 'objet (vrac) … taille fausse … faute du pair'
kept.evidence: service.go:641-655: a final slice with another size returns ErrSizeMismatch and is not a fault, and :493-496 d.discard() deletes the download; a non-final one triggers confirmSize (:676-702), which sends a second WANT for the last group of the claimed size, faults only on 'refuted', and on BUSY, silence or MISSING only strikes (:654). poc_test.go:64-93 pins that an honest BUSY peer is not faulted under a lying index.
kept.scenario: A Byzantine writer puts a wrong size into the project index. A third-party requester following the spec text faults every honest holder (size ≠ expected) and bans each one after 3 blobs, so the blob becomes unreachable everywhere. Go instead uses an extra, undocumented WANT exchange. In the other direction, a peer that lies about the size in non-final slices and answers the confirmation with BUSY is never faulted. Two conformant implementations disagree on who is at fault.
kept.fix: Write the confirmation rule into §8.1 (the last-group proof, what proven, refuted and unproven mean, and that an authenticated final size over-rules the index), with vectors. Or change the code to the spec, after deciding how a lying index is handled under the Byzantine-writer threat model.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. In accept (service.go:641-655), a final slice with another size returns ErrSizeMismatch with no fault, and fetch then calls d.discard() (service.go:493-496). A non-final mismatch triggers confirmSize (service.go:676-702), an extra WANT for the last group that the spec does not describe; only 'refuted' is a fault, and BUSY, silence or MISSING lead only to strike(). The spec §8.1 and the §13 row 'objet (vrac)' make a wrong size a fault of the peer. A third-party implementation that follows the spec would blame honest holders when a Byzantine writer puts a wrong size in the index, so the two implementations disagree on who gets banned.

Confirmed. service.go:641-655 and confirmSize (:676-702) implement an undocumented extra WANT for the last group. They fault only on 'refuted', strike on BUSY, MISSING or silence, and a final slice of another size gives ErrSizeMismatch and d.discard (:493-496) with no fault. Spec §8.1 and §13 ('objet (vrac) … taille fausse → faute du pair') say any size mismatch is a fault. Under a Byzantine writer's lying index (a writer can edit the index), a spec-literal requester faults and bans honest holders, and the confirmation sub-exchange appears nowhere in the spec (grep 'confirm' in spec.md finds nothing for §8). This is both a code-to-spec gap and a spec defect.

kept.title: Unsolicited answers are never counted as faults
kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: §8.1 'Un SLICE, MISSING ou BUSY sans demande en cours pour (pair, hash) est non sollicité : jeté sans vérifier Bao ; c'est une faute seulement si aucune demande de ce hash n'a été annulée … depuis 60 s (#slice-unsolicited)'
kept.evidence: service.go:267-274 deliver: 'if w == nil { v.log.Debug("blob: unsolicited answer" …); return }'; nothing records cancelled requests or their time. Vector slice-unsolicited is 'proposed', enforce step-5, decoder 'bulk+expect' not implemented (reference.go:31-49).
kept.scenario: A member streams SLICE frames of ~1 MiB for hashes nobody asked for, at its full flow-control rate. The host reads, allocates and decodes each one and drops it, and the peer never reaches MaxFaults.
kept.fix: Keep for each (peer, hash) the time of the last cancelled request (bounded at 2 per peer). Count an unsolicited answer as a fault when there is none within 60 s. Implement 'bulk+expect' and enforce the vector at step 5.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. deliver (service.go:267-274) only logs at Debug and returns when no waiter exists, and nothing records cancelled requests, so the spec's fault for an unsolicited answer (no cancellation in 60 s) is never applied. Lowered to minor: an unsolicited SLICE is only wire-decoded (blob.Decode, no Bao pass, which the spec allows). The real cost is reading frames, already bounded by flow control and the bulk budget (finding 0).

Partly confirmed. deliver (service.go:267-274) drops an answer with no waiter and never records a fault, and nothing tracks cancelled requests or the 60 s window of §8.1 (#slice-unsolicited, proposed/step-5). One part of the claim is wrong: Bao is not decoded for an unsolicited slice. Only the wire Decode runs (service.go:214); Bao verification happens in accept and checkSlice, which an unsolicited slice never reaches, so the code already does 'jeté sans vérifier Bao'. Impact is bounded by the peer's own bandwidth and the shared budget (N-6). Minor.

kept.title: BUSY handling departs from the spec (wait capped at 5 s, off-by-one count never reset, 8 attempts across peers instead of 3 per holder), and the tests pin these departures
kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: §8.1 'le demandeur attend retry_ms et redemande. Cinq BUSY de suite sur la même plage comptent pour un échec'; 'Trois échecs sur une plage : on la demande à un autre détenteur'; §16.1 'vrac (demandeur) … 3 échecs par plage ; 5 BUSY de suite'
kept.evidence: service.go:38 'maxBusyWait = 5 * time.Second' and :593 'sleep(ctx, min(m.Retry, maxBusyWait))'; :589-591 '*busy++; *busy > maxBusy' makes the 6th BUSY the failure, and busy (declared :532) is never reset by a non-BUSY answer; :34 'maxAttempts = 8' across all peers per range (:533-551). service_limits_test.go:43-67 TestBusyWaitIsCapped asserts the 5 s cap for a 60 s BUSY; :15-41 TestFetchRequestsAreBounded asserts 5+8.
kept.scenario: A conformant server asks for 60 s with BUSY. Go asks again after 5 s, so the server spends its BUSY budget on Go's re-asks and then goes silent. With 10 holders that each fail once, Go gives up after 8 attempts (ErrNoPeer) although the spec moves to the next holder only after 3 failures at the same one.
kept.fix: Wait the full retry_ms (it is ≤ 60 s by decoding). Count 5 consecutive BUSY, reset by any other answer. Count failures per (range, holder) with protocol.BulkRangeFailures. Rewrite the two tests to the spec rule, by name.

verdicts.reason: Partly confirmed. service.go:38 and :593 cap the wait at min(m.Retry, 5 s), against the spec's 'attend retry_ms'. busy (declared in pull, service.go:532) is never reset by a non-BUSY answer, and the failure comes at *busy > 5 (service.go:589-591), so the BUSY are not counted 'de suite' and the count is off by one. The 8-attempt cap across peers (service.go:34, :533) is an extra bound the spec does not state. The '3 failures per holder' reading is not supported: the spec says 'Trois échecs sur une plage', and Go moving to other holders sooner is not a violation. Lowered to minor: the impact is on interoperability with a third-party server.

Confirmed divergences. maxBusyWait = 5 s caps the wait (service.go:38, :593; a retry_ms up to 60 000 is allowed by §8.1). '*busy++; *busy > maxBusy' makes the 6th BUSY the failure (:589-591), and busy is declared per pull (:532) and never reset by a non-BUSY answer, against '5 BUSY de suite'. maxAttempts = 8 across peers (:34, :533-551) replaces '3 échecs par plage … autre détenteur'. TestBusyWaitIsCapped (service_limits_test.go:44) and TestFetchRequestsAreBounded (:17) pin these. Minor: Go servers always send Retry 1 s, so the harm is interoperability with a third-party server and the BUSY budget.

kept.title: Malformed bulk frames are faults, not connection violations, and are ignored entirely while the peer is banned; faults never age
kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: §13 'connexion | toute trame ou tout préambule mal formé, sur tout flux (sync, vrac) … | GOAWAY PROTOCOL_VIOLATION, fermeture, Tenu'; §8.1 'Une trame mal formée (décodage) est une violation'; '3 fautes en 10 min, on ne l'interroge plus pendant 10 min'
kept.evidence: service.go:214-217 a Decode error goes to misbehaved; :312-317 'if until, ok := v.banned[peer]; ok && time.Now().Before(until) { v.mu.Unlock(); return }' so during a ban a fault is neither counted nor acted on; :318-324 faults[peer]++ with no time window; :329-331 Drop → node.go:681-691 (unwant, ClosePeer, forgetAddrs) deletes 'held', so the member can reconnect at once.
kept.scenario: A member sends 3 malformed frames and is dropped. It reconnects at once (Admit accepts it, and Drop removed the backoff), then sends malformed bulk frames of up to 64 MiB for 10 minutes with no consequence, since misbehaved returns early. Under the spec the first malformed frame closes the connection with Tenu backoff. Conversely, a peer with 3 faults spread over days is banned, which the spec does not ask.
kept.fix: Treat a decode error on the bulk stream as a violation of that connection (reset plus Tenu) in p2p, before the Service. Keep content faults (Bao, size, unsolicited) in a sliding 10-minute window. During a ban, still act on violations.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. A Decode error goes to misbehaved (service.go:214-217) as a fault, not as a connection violation with Tenu (§13 row 'connexion', §8.1 'trame mal formée … violation'). misbehaved returns early while the peer is banned (service.go:312-317), so nothing is counted or acted on during the ban. faults[peer]++ has no time window (service.go:318-324), against the spec's '3 fautes en 10 min'. Drop (node.go:681-691) runs delete(n.held, id), so a member dropped for faults can reconnect at once, since Admit still accepts it.

Confirmed. A Decode error goes to misbehaved (service.go:214-217), a fault, while §8.1 and §13 make a malformed bulk frame a connection violation with Tenu backoff. During a ban, misbehaved returns early (:312-317), so nothing is counted or acted on. faults[peer]++ has no 10-minute window (:318-324). Drop (node.go:681-691) deletes held and, per its own doc comment, leaves a still-admitted peer free to reconnect at once. A member can therefore keep sending malformed bulk frames after its drop with no further consequence until the ban ends.

kept.title: Slice verification and extraction live in the application, not in protocol/blob; internal/blob keeps private copies of codec rules
kept.question: go-equals-ts
kept.rule: CLAUDE.md invariant 'inkwell importe protocol et n'a aucune copie privée de ses codecs'; spec §1.6/§21 'ses codecs sont ceux de ces paquets'; README point 8 (reusable by a third party)
kept.evidence: internal/blob/service.go:737-765 checkSlice (bao header, range rules, final-group rule, bao.DecodeSlice) and store.go:621-660 extractSlice (the Bao slice encoder) exist only in the application; protocol/blob/wire.go has framing only. internal/blob/protocol.go:55 'maxOffset = 1 << 40' duplicates wire.go:26, and :59-62 'func checkRange(offset uint64, length uint32, _ bool)' re-implements the range rule and silently ignores its exact flag (it always encodes a Want). No TypeScript implementation exists, so no Go/TS comparison is possible.
kept.scenario: A third party that reuses protocol/blob gets no slice verifier and must re-implement the §8.1 Bao and final-group rules from prose. inkwell's own verifier is not what the conformance runner exercises. A future checkRange(…, false) caller in internal/blob would get the exact (Want) rule without noticing.
kept.fix: Move VerifySlice(h, want, slice, expectedSize) and EncodeSlice into protocol/blob, used by internal/blob, and delete the private maxOffset and checkRange. Give it a conformance decoder (see the proof finding).

verdicts.reason: Partly confirmed. checkSlice (service.go:737-765) and the Bao slice extraction live only in internal/blob, and protocol/blob has framing only (wire.go). So a third party reusing protocol gets no slice verifier, which weakens README point 8. This is a missing codec in protocol, not a private copy of an existing one, except the duplicated maxOffset (protocol.go:55 next to wire.go:26). checkRange's ignored exact flag (protocol.go:59-62) has one caller, store.go:582, which passes true, so no defect today. Comparing Go and TypeScript is moot: blobs are Go-only by design. Minor.

Confirmed but over-rated. checkSlice (service.go:737-765) and extractSlice (store.go:621-660) exist only in internal/blob; protocol/blob/wire.go has framing only, so a third party gets no slice verifier (README point 8). internal/blob/protocol.go:55 duplicates maxOffset (wire.go:26), and checkRange (:59-62) ignores its exact flag by always encoding a Want. Its only caller today passes exact = true (store.go:582), so there is no live bug. These are not copies of a protocol codec but rules missing from the protocol module. Minor.

kept.title: The vectors cover framing only: Bao verification is in no vector, and slice-final-group's expectations are never checked
kept.question: proof
kept.rule: README point 8 'des vecteurs de conformité … qu'une implémentation tierce exécute sans inkwell'; §21 'reproduit chaque expect'; §8.1 'il se vérifie contre le seul hash (bulk.json#slice-final-group : 8 + 64 + 4464 octets)'
kept.evidence: conformance/reference.go:227-235 bulk() only runs Decode and Encode; verify() (:157-180) asserts only blake3_hex, so slice-final-group's expect {length 4464, bao_total 70000, bao_len 4536} (cmd/vectors/main.go:416-419) is ignored. bulk.json has no vector with a forged or bit-flipped bao, a wrong hash, k=65, length 0, an unaligned offset, bao > 1 064 960, retry_ms 60 001, an unknown kind or trailing bytes (those exist only as Go unit tests, protocol/blob/wire_test.go:26-61). internal/blob/poc_fuzz_test.go:5-27 fuzzes random bao bytes against a fixed hash, so acceptance is unreachable and the fuzzer cannot show that a valid slice for another range or size is refused. Verdicts are produced by the code under test (main.go:410-424 'Verdict: verdict(err)').
kept.scenario: An implementation that never verifies Bao, or that miscomputes the final-group length, passes every bulk vector and the conformance runner.
kept.fix: Add a 'bulk_slice+verify' decoder (context: outstanding want and expected size), with accept, forged-parent, forged-data, wrong-size, short-slice and wrong-offset vectors. Assert every expect key, and fail on unknown keys. Add vectors for each wire bound at the bound and at bound + 1. Make the fuzzer start from a valid slice and mutate one byte or field, expecting rejection.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. bulk() (reference.go:227-235) only runs blob.Decode and blob.Encode. verify() (reference.go:157-180) checks the verdict, the round trip and blake3_hex only. slice-final-group's expect {length, bao_total, bao_len} (main.go:416-419) is never read, and bulk has no generic expect loop like the one at reference.go:342. No bulk vector exercises Bao verification. The verdicts are computed by the code under test (main.go:410-417, verdict(err)). An implementation that skips Bao verification passes every bulk vector.

Confirmed. reference.go bulk() (:227-235) only runs Decode/Encode. verify() (:157-180) checks only the verdict, the round trip and blake3_hex, so slice-final-group's expectations length/bao_total/bao_len (cmd/vectors/main.go:417-418) are checked by nothing (grep finds no other reader of bao_total or bao_len). The bulk.json listing has 10 vectors: framing only, no forged or bit-flipped Bao, and the two bulk+expect vectors are proposed with no decoder. An implementation that never verifies Bao passes every bulk vector.

kept.title: A peer that may not be served gets silence instead of MISSING
kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: §8.1 'un blob de projet n'est servi que si le demandeur est un membre actif non suspendu ; sinon MISSING (indiscernable d'un blob absent)'
kept.evidence: service.go:221-224 'if !v.opt.Allowed(peer) { v.log.Debug(…); return }' sends nothing.
kept.scenario: A suspended member's requester (a conformant third party) waits the full 30 s per range instead of moving on at once. It also learns that it is not allowed, where the spec answer would not tell it.
kept.fix: Answer MISSING (subject to the per-peer BUSY/MISSING rate) or change the spec to silence. Add a named test.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. service.go:221-224 logs at Debug and returns without sending anything for a WANT from a peer that is not Allowed. The spec says MISSING, indistinguishable from an absent blob. The conformant requester waits its 30 s timeout per request, and silence is distinguishable from MISSING.

Confirmed. On a WANT, service.go:221-224 returns without sending when !Allowed(peer). §8.1 says 'sinon MISSING (indiscernable d'un blob absent)'. A suspended member (Role > 0, so admitted at wiring.go:54-57) waits the 30 s timeout per range, and silence tells it apart from absence, which MISSING would not.

kept.title: Wire rules and bounds in the code that §8.1 and §16 do not state
kept.question: code-to-spec
kept.rule: README point 3 'la plage de chaque champ, et ce qu'on fait de chaque valeur hors plage'; §1.3 strict decoding
kept.evidence: protocol/blob/wire.go:25-26 'maxOffset = 1 << 40' refused in checkRange :115 (the spec only says 'offset multiple de 16 384', u64); wire.go:144 and :194 require len(bao) ≥ 8 + length (the spec states only the upper bound); store.go:598-600 a WANT at offset ≥ size is answered MISSING; store.go:51-54 DefaultMaxFile 100 MB and DefaultMaxProject 2 GB bound what is fetched, but §16.1 has no blob-size row; service.go:329-331 together with node.go:686-691 make 3 faults close and unwant the peer for all protocols, where the spec says only 'not asked for 10 min'.
kept.scenario: A spec-conformant peer sending an aligned offset above 2^40 is treated as malformed, which would be a violation, by Go. A third party cannot know the MISSING answer for an out-of-file offset or the 100 MB ceiling.
kept.fix: Add these to §8.1 and §16.1 (offset ≤ 2^40 and bao ≥ 8 + length as decoding rules, the out-of-range WANT answer, the impl. blob-size row, the penalty for 3 faults), with vectors for the decoding rules.

verdicts.reason: Partly confirmed. maxOffset = 1<<40 (wire.go:25-26), enforced in checkRange (wire.go:115), is a bound §8.1 and §16 do not state. The size ceilings at store.go:51-54 and the Drop on MaxFaults (service.go:329-331 → node.go:681-691, which closes every protocol) are also undocumented. The len(bao) ≥ 8+length rule (wire.go:144, :194) is implied by the Bao format, which honest peers always meet, so that sub-claim is weak. Minor.

Partly confirmed. Undocumented on the wire: offset > 2^40 refused by Decode (wire.go:25-26, :115); WANT at offset ≥ file size answered MISSING (store.go:598-600); 3 faults closing the peer on all protocols (service.go:329-331 → node.go:681-691), where the spec says only 'not asked for 10 min'. Refuted part: len(bao) ≥ 8 + length (wire.go:144, :194) follows from the §8.1 description of bao (u64 size, parents, data bytes), so it is not an extra rule. DefaultMaxFile/MaxProject (store.go:51-54) are local storage policy, not a wire bound.

kept.title: No formal model for the stateful bulk part, and no written reason
kept.question: proof
kept.rule: README point 9 'un modèle formel (TLA+ ou Alloy, avec mutants) dès qu'il y a un état ou de la concurrence ; sinon, la raison écrite dans l'ADR'
kept.evidence: docs/protocol/tla and docs/protocol/alloy contain no bulk model (grep 'bulk|vrac|blob' matches only SendPath.tla and tla/README.md as cross traffic); §8.1 lines 1037-1070 claim liveness and fairness properties for ranks and slots ('porte P-BYZ') and §8.1 lines 984-1001 define request matching, BUSY and the fault state machine.
kept.scenario: The fairness and liveness claims, such as 'un flux de nouvelles annonces ne passe jamais devant elle' and 'ni 65 membres successifs … ne dépassent le plafond', rest on prose alone.
kept.fix: Model request matching, BUSY, faults and the server per-peer share (step 5), and the slot/rank queue with the 1 GiB eviction (step 8), with mutants (no reserved share, preemption, rank reset). Or write the reason for not modelling into ADR 0034.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. No TLA+ or Alloy file models bulk: only SendPath.tla, its mutants and tla/README.md mention it, as cross traffic. ADR 0034 (lines 201-202) names one model, RepoGen.tla, without giving a reason to leave out the bulk request, BUSY and fault state machine, which README point 9 requires. The liveness claims about ranks and slots belong to the step-8 indivisible part, which is not implemented. That lowers the urgency, so minor.

Confirmed: grep finds no bulk or blob model in docs/protocol/tla or alloy (only cross-traffic mentions in SendPath.tla:58, :82), and no ADR gives the reason README point 9 requires, although §8.1 defines stateful matching, BUSY and fault rules. Slightly overstated: the indivisible fairness and liveness claims are not prose alone, because ADR 0034:179 lists them as P-BYZ gate scenarios (still to run). Those scenarios are not a formal model with mutants, and they belong to step 8 anyway.

dropped.title: One member, reader or suspended member, or a stranger during the invitation window, can freeze every blob transfer of the host with a 4-byte frame header

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. bulk.go:164-170 calls frame.ReadReserve(s, transport.MaxFrame, ...) with cost = min(size+msgOverhead, bulkBuffered), and bulkBuffered (bulk.go:29) is one MaxFrame shared by every peer. frame.go:77-86 runs reserve(n) right after the 4-byte header and then io.ReadFull blocks on the payload. budget.go:23-29 Acquire waits on a cond with no timeout. The only SetReadDeadline in p2p is lobby.go:69. bulk.go:140 gates only on n.admitted(p), and node.go:530-538 makes that Admit(name) || isOpen(), where Admit = Role(key) > 0 (wiring.go:54-57), so a reader can do it too. A header near 64 MiB followed by silence holds the whole budget, and every other peer's bulk reader then waits in Acquire. Lowered to major: this is inventoried defect N-6 (inventaire.md:69, graded Majeur, scheduled for ADR 0034 step 5), only blob transfers stop (sync is unaffected), and the stranger part is finding 2. What is new is that the attack needs only a header and no payload, and that a reader can do it.

The mechanism is real (bulk.go:27-29 one-frame budget shared by all peers; bulk.go:164-170 Acquire on the header; budget.go:23-29 blocks; no SetReadDeadline except lobby.go:69), but it is already inventoried: docs/protocol/inventaire.md:69 N-6 (Majeur, open) says a member sending a 64 MiB frame slowly stops every file transfer, citing bulk.go:27-30 and :164-168. ADR 0034:224 schedules the fix in step 5 ('vrac : trame ≤ 1 065 005 o, parts par pair', closes N-6). A header followed by nothing is just the extreme case of 'envoie lentement'. Readers and suspended members are members (wiring.go:54-57, Role > 0), so N-6 already covers them. The one new angle, a stranger during the invitation window, is finding [2].

dropped.title: No progress-based deadline and no adaptive request size: slow honest links never complete a range

verdicts.reason: Confirmed, and it restates inventoried defect N-15 (inventaire.md:78, '30 s par WANT de 1 Mio', scheduled for ADR 0034 step 5). defaultTimeout = 30 s (service.go:29) is set once at send (service.go:373) and covers the whole answer. The bulk lane delivers only whole frames (bulk.go:164-178). download.next (partial.go:132-145) always asks for up to MaxSlice/GroupSize groups, with no adaptive size. On a link slow enough that 1 MiB takes over 30 s, every attempt fails although bytes keep arriving.

Already inventoried. docs/protocol/inventaire.md:78 N-15 (Majeur) says that the rate-based deadlines ('30 s par WANT de 1 Mio') make an honest peer behind a slow relay fail in a loop, citing blob/service.go. The fix (§8.1 'délai au progrès, tailles adaptatives') is assigned to ADR 0034 step 5 (adr/0034:224, closes N-15). The finding itself says 'Already inventoried as N-15' and adds no new mechanism: service.go:29, :373 and partial.go next() are exactly the inventoried behaviour.

No peer can announce such a change today, so there is no reachable defect, only scheduled work.

Not a reachable defect: it is unbuilt, tracked future work. The finding itself says 'Not reachable today'. The indivisible vectors in repo.json are 'proposed' with enforce step-8, and ADR 0034's migration table schedules ADR 0031 objects and SET for step 8 (adr/0034:228). serve's Referenced-only check (service.go:282-297) is the correct current behaviour while no peer announces indivisible changes. Treat it as planned work for step 8, not an audit finding.

kept.title: During an invitation window a stranger is fully admitted to the sync and bulk streams, not only the lobby
kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: spec §5.1 (spec.md:591-592): « Un pair qui n'est pas membre mais que la fenêtre d'invitation laisse se connecter ne peut ouvrir que /inkwell/lobby/1.0.0 ; tout autre flux de sa part est réinitialisé » ; §12 step 1 (spec.md:1985): « membre, ou fenêtre d'invitation pour le salon seul » ; threat model: unattested peers strictly bounded
kept.evidence: internal/transport/p2p/node.go:530-538 `return n.opts.Admit == nil || n.opts.Admit(name) || n.isOpen()`: while the window is open, any authenticated peer is « admitted » for every use. stream.go:47,58 `ps.connected, ps.admitted = true, admitted`, then stream.go:76 startOpenLocked opens the host's outbound sync stream to the stranger and announces it up. stream.go:234 `if !n.admitted(p) { return }` accepts the stranger's inbound /inkwell/sync/1.0.0 streams, which read frames up to transport.MaxFrame into the node-wide 256 MiB budget (node.go:119, stream.go:262-271). bulk.go:140 does the same for bulk streams, against the single-frame budget shared by all peers (bulk.go:29,61,164-181). The only filter is in the app: wiring.go:424 and :396 drop the frames of peers that are not linked or active. lobby_test.go:109-149 (TestOpenWindow) only tests the lobby; nothing checks that the other streams are reset.
kept.scenario: An admin issues a ticket, which opens the window for 15 min (flow.go:263-281 → invites.go:179-183 → SetOpen). Any device that learns the host's PeerID and address (mDNS announces both, spec §18) connects. Its sync stream is accepted and the host opens its own sync stream to it. It then streams frames of up to ~64 MiB on the sync and bulk lanes. The host allocates and buffers them, up to its 256 MiB budget, and competes for the bulk lane's single global frame budget with the members' blob transfers, until the app drops them. The joiner opens the same window to everyone (invites.go:196-200, 352), so the same applies to a device that is joining.
kept.fix: In the transport, refuse every protocol but the lobby from a peer admitted only by the window. Keep two predicates: member (Options.Admit) and stranger (isOpen). Use the stranger one only in handleLobbyStream and the gater; handleStream, handleBulk and onConnected/startOpenLocked must require the member one. Add a test that a stranger in the window has its sync and bulk streams reset and gets no PeerUp, and a vector or a netsim case if wanted.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. node.go:530-538 admitted() returns true for any valid, non-held peer while isOpen(); stream.go:47-58 sets ps.admitted and startOpenLocked (stream.go:76-81) opens the host's sync stream; openOut then calls Protect(memberTag) and pushes PeerUp (stream.go:111-116), so the stranger is also shielded from the connection manager. The inbound sync handler (stream.go:234) and the bulk handler (bulk.go:140) gate only on admitted(), and frames are reserved against the node budget (stream.go:262-271) before the app drops them (wiring.go:396 isActive, :424 isLinked). Spec §5.1 (spec.md:591-592) says every stream other than the lobby is reset. This is reachable today: ShareDialog calls Invite, the ticket opens the window (flow.go:263-281 → invites.go:179-183). It is not among the known findings (IV1 covers flow.go:411-427 and :371-383).

Confirmed. node.go:530-538 admitted() returns true for any valid key while isOpen(); stream.go:47-58 sets ps.admitted and startOpenLocked opens the host's sync stream; stream.go:234 and bulk.go:140 accept the stranger's inbound sync and bulk streams on the same check. frame.go:77-86 ReadReserve reserves the announced size before reading the body, so one stranger announcing a ~64 MiB bulk frame and trickling bytes holds the whole bulk budget (bulk.go:27-29, one MaxFrame for all peers). The only filter is in the app after delivery (wiring.go:395 isActive, :423 isLinked). This breaks spec §17 (spec.md:2135-2136, « Les inconnus ne parlent qu'au salon ») and §12 step 1 (spec.md:1985). §5.1 itself describes the 2.0 session, but §17 and §12 cover the code that runs today. The webview side of the same cause was noted in the old audit S1-R6 (docs/plans/audit-2026-10-31/06-admission-design.md:438). That is not one of the listed known findings, and the transport-level admission is still open.

kept.title: Ask: the joiner never authenticates the host, so a visible LAN device can pose as a project
kept.question: hostile-peer
kept.rule: spec §8.2 (spec.md:1107-1112) says only « Ask attend l'accord d'une personne », with no host authentication for the joiner; README point 6 (security considerations under a full Byzantine threat model); invariant « tout octet venu d'un pair est vérifié »
kept.evidence: internal/invite/flow.go:501-511: for Ask « The project is not known in advance, so it is only checked to be coherent: the host's own genesis certifies it, and the person who accepted compared fingerprints ». The only fingerprint built is the joiner's, shown to the host (flow.go:389, 402). The joiner sees only the self-asserted Hello: flow.go:475-484 returns Machine and Title; internal/app/invites.go:82-89 NearbyPerson has Peer, Machine and Title and no host fingerprint; invites.go:424-454 lists any device that answers Hello. verify(rep, host, nil, nil) (flow.go:510) accepts any genesis in which the host is admin and the joiner is a member (flow.go:540-562).
kept.scenario: A hostile device on the LAN stays « visible » and answers Hello with the Machine and Title of a real nearby project. The person picks it from the list and sends Ask. The hostile host adds the joiner to its own genesis at once and returns a Welcome that passes verify. The joiner adopts the attacker's project as if it were the one it wanted, and everything the person then writes goes to the attacker.
kept.fix: Make Ask mutual: show the joiner the host's four-word fingerprint, derived from the host PeerID it is connected to, and have both people compare both fingerprints (or one short code derived from both keys, as in SAS or PAKE pairing) before the joiner adopts. Write the obligation into §8.2 as a DOIT, add a named test with an impostor host, and a mutant that skips the host check.

verdicts.reason: The gap is real: Joiner.Ask (flow.go:501-511) calls verify(rep, host, nil, nil), which only checks that the Welcome is coherent (flow.go:540-562). The only fingerprint shown is the joiner's, to the host (flow.go:389-402). NearbyPerson (invites.go:82-89) carries only the self-asserted Machine and Title from Hello (flow.go:475-484). So the joiner cannot authenticate the host. Lowered to minor because no peer can reach it in the app today: frontend/src never calls Session.Nearby, Ask or SetVisible (grep finds them only in the generated bindings), so the Ask path cannot be triggered from the interface. It stays a protocol-design gap in §8.2 for any future UI or third-party joiner. It is not the W58 or JN1 items, which are about adoption races and local provenance.

Confirmed. In flow.go:501-511, Ask calls verify(rep, host, nil, nil): no project and no person are expected. verify (flow.go:530-570) only checks that the Welcome holds together: the host is admin of the genesis it sent, and the joiner is a member. The only fingerprint is the joiner's, made in addAsk (flow.go:391, 402) and shown on the host. NearbyPerson (invites.go:82-89) carries only the self-declared Peer, Machine and Title from Hello (invites.go:446-452). No host fingerprint is shown in the frontend: no svelte file mentions one. No other check stops a LAN stranger from posing as a project. It is not in the known findings: IV1 covers refusal state and Ask lifetime only.

kept.title: The ticket decoder does not check that the host is a valid key, nor that the addresses are multiaddrs
kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: spec §3.2 (spec.md:229-233): every key DOIT be validated « au plus tôt, à chaque point d'entrée … hôte d'un ticket » ; §8.3 (spec.md:1121-1124): `host str8 (PeerID, clé valide §3.2)`, `naddr × str8 (multiaddr sans « /p2p/<host> »)` ; §1.3: a value out of its domain DOIT be refused
kept.evidence: protocol/invite/ticket.go:168 `if !transport.ValidPeerID(t.Host) || strings.Contains(string(t.Host), "/")`. ValidPeerID (protocol/peer.go:16-26) checks only 1 to 64 printable ASCII bytes: no multihash decoding, no Ed25519 or small-order check. ticket.go:190-197 validAddr accepts any printable ASCII that starts with « / », including addresses that already contain /p2p/<other>. The key is first checked only later, when dialling (gate.go:37 KeyFromID) and in Joiner.verify (flow.go:533-539). lobby.json has no ticket vector with an invalid host.
kept.scenario: ParseText accepts `inkwell1:`+base32 of a ticket whose host is « AAAA » or the PeerID of a small-order key (crypto.json#peer-id-small-order), and whose addresses are « /x ». The app treats it as valid: it shows it, checks its expiry and dials (invites.go:302-321). The refusal comes only later, from the transport, with a dial or handshake error instead of « malformed ticket ». A third-party implementation that follows the decoder as written has no key check at all on this entry point.
kept.fix: In decodeTicket, decode the PeerID to its Ed25519 key with a pure decoder in the protocol module (identity multihash plus the protobuf key) and run sig.ValidatePublicKey on it. Parse each address as a multiaddr without a /p2p component. Add reject vectors (invalid host, small-order host, address with /p2p, address that is not a multiaddr) and mutants for both checks.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. ticket.go:168 checks the host only with ValidPeerID (protocol/peer.go:16-26: 1 to 64 printable ASCII bytes) plus no '/'. validAddr (ticket.go:190-197) accepts any printable ASCII that starts with '/'. Spec §3.2 (spec.md:229-233) names « hôte d'un ticket » as an entry point where the key is validated. Lowered to minor: the invalid key is still refused before any trust is given, by Connect's parseID (node.go:633-637), by gate.InterceptSecured → KeyFromID (gate.go:37), and by Joiner.verify's ValidatePublicKey (flow.go:533-539). The effect is a late, less precise error and a decoder that is non-conformant for third parties, not a security exposure.

The gap is real. ticket.go:168 uses only ValidPeerID (peer.go:16-26: 1 to 64 printable ASCII bytes), while spec.md:229-233 requires the key check « au plus tôt … hôte d'un ticket ». validAddr (ticket.go:190-197) only checks printable ASCII and a leading '/'. Lowered to minor because nothing can be exploited: the connection gater (gate.go:37 KeyFromID) and Joiner.verify (flow.go:533-539 ValidatePublicKey) refuse an invalid key before any trust, so the only effect is a late and less clear error. A '/p2p/<relay>' segment inside an address is also legitimate for circuit addresses, so that sub-claim is weak.

kept.title: The Go codec and the TypeScript reference accept different lobby and ticket bytes
kept.question: go-equals-ts
kept.rule: brief question 3: the same accepted and refused bytes, the same limits ; spec §20.7 (spec.md:2254) reasons 1-5 ; §8.3 ticket fields
kept.evidence: frontend/packages/protocol/reference.ts:221 `assert(reason >= 1 && reason <= 4)`, against protocol/invite/lobby.go:200 `rep.Reason < ReasonInvalid || rep.Reason > ReasonTooLarge` (1-5). Ticket: reference.ts:457 `host.length > 0 && host.length <= 64` (any bytes), against ticket.go:168 (printable ASCII, no « / »). reference.ts:460 checks only the first byte « / » of each address, against ticket.go:192-196 (all printable ASCII). reference.ts:455 `r.u64()` has no bound, against ticket.go:158 `exp > 1<<62` refused. lobby.json contains none of these inputs (only accept vectors; Refused is only reason 1), so both runners pass.
kept.scenario: Refused with reason 5 (TooLarge, which the host really sends, flow.go:423-425) is `0305`: Go accepts it, TS rejects it. A ticket whose host is « a/b », or whose address is « /\u0001 », or whose expiry is 2^63 is accepted by TS and rejected by Go. A third-party implementation validated against one reference disagrees with the other.
kept.fix: Align the TS reference with the spec: reasons 1-5, host as a valid PeerID with a valid key (same rule as the fixed Go), addresses as multiaddrs, and the expiry bound either written into §8.3 or removed in Go. Add the reject vectors that make each divergence fail in CI.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed by reading frontend/packages/protocol/reference.ts. At :221 it asserts reason 1..4 while lobby.go:200 and spec §20.7 (spec.md:2254) allow 1..5. At :457 the host check is length only, against ticket.go:168 (printable ASCII, no '/'). At :460 only the first byte of each address is checked, against ticket.go:192-196. At :455 u64 is unbounded, against ticket.go:158. lobby.json has no vector exercising these inputs. Lowered to minor: reference.ts is a test-side conformance runner (its header says so), and the lobby runs only in Go in inkwell, so no shipped component disagrees. The impact is on third parties who validate against the TS runner.

Confirmed. reference.ts:221 has assert(reason >= 1 && reason <= 4), while Go lobby.go:200 accepts 1-5 and §20.7 (spec.md:2254) lists 5 TooLarge. So the TS reference refuses a refusal the host really sends (flow.go:423-425). The host check at reference.ts:457 is by length only, against ticket.go:168 (printable ASCII, no '/'). reference.ts:460 checks only the first byte of each address. reference.ts:455 does not bound the expiry, against ticket.go:158. Lowered to minor: reference.ts is test-side only (header line 2, « Test-side reference »), not production code. Its lack of detection comes from the missing refusal vectors (finding 4), but the divergence itself is a separate defect.

kept.title: The lobby has accept-only vectors, no model and no recorded mutation score
kept.question: proof
kept.rule: README points 8 and 9 (conformance vectors, a fuzzed decoder; a formal model as soon as there is state or concurrency, or the reason written in the ADR) ; brief question 4: each rule has a vector, a named test and a mutant
kept.evidence: protocol/vectors/lobby.json has six vectors, all `"verdict": "accept"`. The generator (protocol/cmd/vectors/main.go:437-451) emits no refusal: no unknown kind, no trailing bytes, no reason 0 or 6, no root_url of 513, no n of 1025, no oversize request or reply, no bad ticket version, flags, role, zero secret, naddr of 17 or expiry. There is no Hello reply vector and no Refused reason 2-5. There is no Welcome+verify vector for the joiner's rules (genesis = ticket project, chain from genesis); those are held only by Go tests (flow_test.go:360 TestJoinerVerifiesProject). Neither docs/protocol/tla nor alloy has a lobby or ticket model, and ADR 0032 gives no reason. gates/C5S/SIMPLIFY.md:84-87 records that `protocol/invite` has older survivors « owned by their packages' blocks and the protocol audit PA », with no score or justification recorded.
kept.scenario: A mutant that drops `r.done()` in DecodeRequest (lobby.go:90), or widens the reason range, or removes the `exp > 1<<62` check, survives every vector, because no vector expects a refusal. A third-party implementation that accepts everything also passes lobby.json. The single-use ticket and the window and Ask states (concurrent Redeem, window closing during an Ask) have no model to check them.
kept.fix: Generate reject vectors for every §1.3 and §8.2/§8.3 rule, plus each reason, the Hello reply and a Welcome+verify case. Run gremlins on protocol/invite and record the score and any equivalent mutants in the IV1 SIMPLIFY.md. Either write a small TLA+ model (ticket single use, window open and close, Ask wait, sweep) or record in ADR 0032 why none is needed.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. lobby.json has six vectors, all « accept » (grep), and the generator protocol/cmd/vectors/main.go:437-451 emits no refusal. docs/protocol/tla and docs/protocol/alloy contain no lobby, ticket or invitation model. gates/C5S/SIMPLIFY.md:84-87 defers the protocol/invite survivors to PA with no score recorded. One part of the scenario is overstated: Go unit tests do kill some of the named mutants. TestLobbyDecodeRejects has « hello trailing » and « bad reason » 99 (protocol/invite/lobby_test.go:40-68), and TestParseTextRejects covers trailing data. Other mutants are untested: a reason range widened to 6, and the removal of the exp > 1<<62 check. The proof gap for third parties holds (no refusal vector, no model, no recorded mutation score), and these are bytes that come from a stranger.

Confirmed. protocol/vectors/lobby.json has six vectors, all « accept » (ticket-text, three lobby requests, welcome, refused). docs/protocol/tla and docs/protocol/alloy have no lobby, ticket or invite model, and ADR 0032 gives no reason. gates/C5S/SIMPLIFY.md:84-87 leaves the protocol/invite survivors to « the protocol audit PA », with no score: that is this audit, so the finding belongs here and is not a duplicate. IV1 (complete rigour) may add a model later, but nothing exists today.

kept.title: The invitation window has no bound or reserved share for strangers: Sybil keys fill the inbound connections and the 8 Ask slots
kept.question: hostile-peer
kept.rule: README rule 4 « Chacun sa part : tout plafond partagé garantit une part à chaque pair » ; README point 5 (flooding, rate limits) ; spec §16.1 only bounds lobby streams per peer (spec.md:2064, 2067), with no total for strangers
kept.evidence: gate.go:36-47 lets in any valid key while the window is open (admit = node.admitted, node.go:530-538). The resource manager gives System ConnsInbound = maxPeers = 64 to members and strangers together (node.go:91, 486-490), with no stranger sub-limit and no reserved share for members. internal/invite/flow.go:28-29 `maxAsks = 8`; addAsk (flow.go:388-406) refuses beyond 8 and allows only one per PeerID, but PeerIDs cost nothing; each Ask waits AskTimeout = 2 min (flow.go:26, 371-383).
kept.scenario: While the host is visible (10 min), an attacker on the LAN opens 64 connections with 64 fresh keys: members dialling in are refused until the window ends. With 8 of those keys it sends Ask: every honest Ask gets Refused Busy (flow.go:363-364), the admin sees 8 fake pending requests, and the attacker repeats every 2 min. For a third-party host that follows only the spec, nothing bounds the number of waiting Asks at all (only 4 streams per peer for 3 min).
kept.fix: Specify in §16.1 a total for stranger connections and lobby streams (for example 8 strangers, never taken from the members' share), a pending-Ask bound, and a per-source rate limit (for example per IP prefix). Reserve inbound connection capacity for members: a stranger limit inside the resource manager, or a separate limiter in the gater. Test that a member can still connect while the stranger slots are full.

verdicts.reason: The connection part holds. newResourceManager gives System ConnsInbound = maxPeers (node.go:486-490) to members and strangers alike, the spec table itself gives no reserved share (spec.md:2062), and strangers that reach PeerUp are Protect'ed like members (stream.go:116), so the connection manager does not trim them. Lowered to minor for three reasons. (1) The Ask-slot part cannot be reached from the app today: Hello and Ask are served only while Visible (flow.go:296-303), and no frontend code calls SetVisible. (2) Outbound dials to members use a separate ConnsOutbound limit, and members already connected keep their connections. (3) It is bounded by the 15-minute ticket window and needs network reachability to the host.

The Ask part holds. maxAsks = 8 (flow.go:28), addAsk refuses beyond that with one Ask per PeerID (flow.go:392-400), PeerIDs cost nothing, AskTimeout is 2 min (flow.go:371), and honest Asks get Busy (flow.go:363-364). The 64-connection part is overstated: go-libp2p v0.51 rcmgr limits connections by default to 8 per IPv4 /32 and 8 per IPv6 /56 (conn_limiter.go:33-46), so one LAN host cannot take all 64 inbound slots. It would need several addresses. Eight Asks still fit within one IP's 8 connections. Lowered to minor: only a time-boxed denial of the invitation the admin chose to open.

kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: spec §16.1 (spec.md:2056-2057, 2064): « salon 4 » ; « Les bornes sont des constantes exportées de protocol ; un test par ligne vérifie la borne, la borne + 1 et la reprise »
kept.evidence: protocol/limits.go:31-32 `LobbyStreams = 4`; internal/transport/p2p/lobby.go:30-31 `maxLobbyStreams = 2`, used in node.go:503-506. lobby.go:21,24,27,29 also redefine MaxLobbyRequest, MaxLobbyResponse and the 10 s and 3 min timeouts instead of using protocol.MaxLobbyRequest, MaxLobbyReply, LobbyRequestTimeout and LobbyProcessingTimeout (limits.go:37-44). kept.fix: Use the protocol constants in p2p/lobby.go and node.go (LobbyStreams, MaxLobbyRequest, MaxLobbyReply, LobbyRequestTimeout, LobbyProcessingTimeout), or change the spec to 2. Add the bound and bound + 1 test.

The row is not marked « impl. » (spec.md:2053-2054), so it is normative. lobby.go:20-29 also keeps private copies of MaxLobbyRequest, MaxLobbyResponse and both timeouts, instead of the protocol constants (limits.go:37-44). No test checks the bound and bound + 1 for lobby streams.

Confirmed. protocol/limits.go:31-32 has LobbyStreams = 4 and spec §16.1 (spec.md:2064) says « salon 4 », with no « impl. » marker. p2p/lobby.go:30-31 has maxLobbyStreams = 2, used at node.go:503-506. lobby.go:21, 24, 27 and 29 redefine the request and reply bounds and both timeouts instead of using the protocol constants (limits.go:37-44). kept.title: Lobby behaviour that the spec does not describe: host states and bounds, silent resets, joiner checks
kept.question: code-to-spec
kept.rule: README points 4, 5, 7 and 10 (state machine of each role, error handling, interoperability, nothing left to guess) ; spec §8.2 (spec.md:1094-1114)
kept.evidence: Host: VisibleFor = 10 min, AskTimeout = 2 min, maxTickets = 16, maxAsks = 8 and one Ask per peer (flow.go:24-29, 388-406); Hello and Ask while not visible, an undecodable request and an unknown kind get no reply, the stream is reset (flow.go:288-311, lobby.go:77-80); an Ask from a member returns a Welcome at once (flow.go:359-360). Joiner window: joinWindow = 2 min, open to every stranger, not only the ticket host (internal/app/invites.go:22-24, 196-209). Joiner checks the spec does not require: no pending or repeated ops, root_url equal to the genesis one, host admin, joiner a member, person match (flow.go:553-570). An unknown future Refused reason is a decode error (lobby.go:200-202), and §20.7 gives no rule for unknown values.
kept.scenario: A third-party host written from §8.2 may answer Refused instead of resetting, have no Ask bound, or keep tickets forever. A third-party joiner written from §8.2 accepts a Welcome where it is not a member, or where the host is not an admin. Adding reason 6 later breaks every inkwell joiner, which reads it as malformed.
kept.fix: Add to §8.2 the host and joiner state machines with their timers and bounds (and the §16.1 rows), the rule « no answer = stream reset » for unserved and malformed requests, the full list of joiner DOIT checks, and a rule for unknown reasons (for example, treat as Invalid). Say in the spec that the joiner window is limited to the expected host, and limit it in code (invites.go:196).

verdicts.reason: Confirmed as gaps between spec and code. Spec §8.2 (spec.md:1094-1114) gives no visible duration, Ask timeout, bound on Asks or tickets, or rule for answering versus resetting. The code has VisibleFor, AskTimeout, maxTickets and maxAsks (flow.go:22-29), resets on decode error, unknown kind or not visible (flow.go:288-311), and answers a member's Ask with an immediate Welcome (flow.go:359-360). The joiner's extra checks (flow.go:553-570: no pending or repeated ops, root_url, host admin, joiner member) are not required by §8.2, which asks only for the chain, the keys and the genesis = project. §20.7 gives no rule for an unknown reason, which lobby.go:200-202 treats as malformed. It overlaps findings 5 and 11 in places, but its content is distinct: role behaviour, not framing or resources.

Mostly confirmed. Spec §8.2 (spec.md:1107-1114) does not give VisibleFor, AskTimeout, maxTickets, maxAsks or the one-Ask-per-peer rule (flow.go:21-29, 388-406). It does not say that an undecodable request, an unknown kind or a Hello or Ask while not visible are reset (flow.go:288-311). Nor does it require the joiner checks the code applies: host is admin, joiner is a member, root_url matches, no pending or repeated ops (flow.go:553-562). One sub-claim is refuted: §1.3 (spec.md:32-34) already says to refuse a value out of its domain, so refusing an unknown reason is specified behaviour, and adding a reason is an incompatible change, not a gap. The Ask-bound part overlaps finding 5.

kept.title: Name bounds disagree: CleanName keeps 40 runes, but an op name holds at most 128 bytes, so the Add fails after the ticket is consumed
kept.question: spec-to-code
kept.rule: IV1 rule « a refusal changes no state » (ultrareview-admission-invite, disposition IV1) ; spec §8.2 Redeem « puis signe l'ajout du nouvel appareil »
kept.evidence: internal/identity/device.go:29 `maxMachineNameRunes = 40` and :204-216 CleanName cut by runes; protocol/trust/op.go:27-28 `MaxName = 128` bytes, checked in validate (op.go:203), which List.build calls (list.go:409). internal/invite/flow.go:322 take() removes the ticket before admit (flow.go:329); admit (flow.go:413-418) returns Refused Failed when Issue fails.
kept.scenario: A person whose device name is 33 to 40 four-byte letters (for example mathematical bold letters U+1D400, which are IsLetter) redeems a valid ticket. The name is cleaned to up to 160 bytes, validate refuses the Add, the host answers Refused Failed, and the ticket is gone. This is a new trigger of the IV1 rule, not finding 1 (TooLarge).
kept.fix: Make CleanName cut to trust.MaxName bytes on a rune boundary (as appendStr does), or cut the name in admit before Issue. Within IV1, check every rule that can refuse before take() consumes the ticket. Add a test with a 40-rune four-byte name.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. CleanName keeps up to 40 runes of IsLetter or IsDigit (identity/device.go:29, :204-216), so 4-byte letters give up to 160 bytes. Op.validate refuses a Name over MaxName = 128 bytes (protocol/trust/op.go:27-28, :203), and validate is reached from Issue's build (protocol/trust/list.go:409). On Redeem, take() deletes the ticket (flow.go:320-339) before admit's Issue fails and returns Refused Failed (flow.go:413-418). This is a new trigger: the known IV1 finding 1 is the TooLarge check after the Add. Minor: only the joiner's own name sets it off, so a hostile joiner can only waste its own ticket. It is an honest-user failure, not an attack.

Confirmed. CleanName (device.go:204-216) cuts to 40 runes, which can be up to 160 bytes for 4-byte letters. Op.validate refuses Name > MaxName = 128 bytes (op.go:27-28, 203), and List issue calls validate before signing (list.go:409). redeem calls take() (flow.go:322), which removes the ticket before admit, and admit returns Refused Failed when Issue fails (flow.go:413-418). The ticket is lost. The same refusal reaches an accepted Ask. IV1 finding 1 is a different trigger (signing before the TooLarge check), so this is a new trigger of the same rule, not a duplicate. Low likelihood, self-harm only.

kept.title: The ticket text is decoded more leniently than §8.3 and §1.3 allow
kept.question: code-to-spec
kept.rule: spec §8.3 (spec.md:1126-1127): only « la casse, les espaces et les retours à la ligne sont ignorés » ; §1.3 (spec.md:30-38): tolerance only at the planned extension points, `encode(decode(b)) = b`
kept.evidence: protocol/invite/ticket.go:114-119 removes every unicode.IsSpace rune (U+00A0, U+0085, U+2028, U+3000 …); ticket.go:126 `strings.ToUpper` maps non-ASCII letters to base32 letters (U+017F « ſ » → « S », U+0131 « ı » → « I »); with NoPadding, Go's base32 decoder ignores a dangling last character and does not check that the unused bits are zero (GOROOT encoding/base32 base32.go:316-322, 360-380). The TS reference (reference.ts:433-447) does not tolerate case or spaces at all.
kept.scenario: `inkwell1:` + the vector body with one « I » replaced by « ı », or with an extra « A » at the end, is accepted by ParseText as the same ticket. Several texts denote one ticket, and an implementation that follows the spec (strict except for ASCII case and whitespace) refuses texts that inkwell accepts.
kept.fix: Remove only ASCII space, tab, CR and LF; upper-case ASCII only; refuse a body whose length mod 8 is 1, 3 or 6 or whose padding bits are not zero (re-encode and compare). Add the matching reject vectors.

verdicts.reason: Mostly confirmed. ticket.go:114-119 drops every unicode.IsSpace rune, and ticket.go:126 strings.ToUpper maps U+0131 to 'I' and U+017F to 'S'. Go's NoPadding base32 decoder (base32.go:316-322, switch at :360-380) produces no byte and no error for a final quantum of 1, 3 or 6 characters, and never checks the unused bits. One correction: an extra trailing 'A' is accepted only when the body length is a multiple of 8. Otherwise the leftover changes the byte count and decodeTicket's length check refuses it (ticket.go:181). Several texts can denote one ticket. Minor: there is no security impact, since the secret is single-use and checked in constant time.

Confirmed. ticket.go:114-119 strips every unicode.IsSpace rune, not only ASCII space and line breaks. ticket.go:126 strings.ToUpper maps 'ſ' to 'S' and 'ı' to 'I'. Go base32 with NoPadding ends a short final quantum at the end of input without the 1/3/6-length check, which runs only on the padding path (base32.go:316-322 vs 343-345), and does not check the unused bits. A trailing extra character is therefore accepted. The secret is unchanged, so there is no security effect: this is only a conformance deviation from §8.3 (spec.md:1126-1127).

kept.title: Documentation gaps for the lobby: framing, ticket unit, CHANGES entry, stale paths
kept.question: code-to-spec
kept.rule: README points 2, 3 and 10 (a versioned identifier with a CHANGES entry; the byte layout of each message; the text is enough on its own)
kept.evidence: spec.md:1096-1097 says « une trame requête … une trame réponse » without saying the frame is `u32 length || payload` as in §5.2 (the code uses frame.Write and frame.Read: lobby.go:70, 83, 114, 120), whereas §8.1 says so explicitly (spec.md:964). spec.md:1126 « au plus 1024 octets » vs spec.md:2102 « 1024 caractères » (and limits.go:201 « in characters »); the code counts bytes (ticket.go:120). docs/protocol/CHANGES.md has no entry for /inkwell/lobby/1.0.0 or ticket version 1 (grep finds only the N15 row and row 14). docs/protocol/inventaire.md:21-22 cite internal/invite/lobby.go:13-200 and ticket.go:31-200, and ADR 0032 cites internal/invite/ticket.go:36-37: those files no longer exist (the code is in protocol/invite).

CHANGES.md has no lobby or ticket entry (only the N15 row and row 14). inventaire.md:21-22 and ADR 0032:59, :65 cite internal/invite/lobby.go and ticket.go, which no longer exist: ls internal/invite shows only flow.go, protocol.go and wormhole.go plus tests, and the code is in protocol/invite.

Confirmed. §8.2 (spec.md:1096-1097) says « une trame » without the u32 layout, while §8.1 (spec.md:963-964) states it, and the code uses frame.Read and frame.Write (p2p/lobby.go:70). The size limit is « au plus 1024 octets » at spec.md:1126 but « 1024 caractères » at spec.md:2102 and limits.go:200-201. docs/protocol/CHANGES.md mentions the lobby only in rows 53 and 467, with no entry for lobby/1.0.0 or ticket version 1. inventaire.md:21-22 cite internal/invite/lobby.go and ticket.go, and ADR 0032:59 and :65 cite internal/invite/ticket.go. Neither file exists (ls internal/invite shows flow.go, protocol.go, wormhole.go and tests only).

dropped.title: The joiner's window (2 min) ends before the longest Ask (2 min 30 s): the host can sign an Add whose Welcome the joiner has already cut off

verdicts.reason: Duplicate of known finding IV1 #2 (ultrareview-admission-invite.md:11): « an Ask stays acceptable after the visible window ended or the asker left: the admin can sign an Add for a device that will never receive the Welcome ». The joiner's window sweep closing the connection (invites.go:196-200, node.go:575-588) is just one way for the asker to leave. The defect on the host side, that ask() at flow.go:371-383 does not end with the stream, and its consequence are the ones IV1 already owns (rule « an Ask ends with its window and its stream »). It also cannot be reached in the app today: no frontend code calls Session.Ask or SetVisible.

Duplicate of a known finding. Ultrareview admission-invite finding 2 (IV1) is « an Ask stays acceptable after the visible window ended or the asker left: the admin can sign an Add for a device that will never receive the Welcome ». The handler context is the node's (p2p/lobby.go:75 context.WithTimeout(n.ctx, lobbyHandleTimeout)), not the stream's. The joiner's sweep closing the connection is one way the asker leaves. kept.title: Relayed link: the first-hop figure is taken from an arbitrary connection to the relay, not a QUIC one
kept.question: code-to-spec
kept.rule: Annex A.1: « Chemin `relayed` : `lossPermille` est le chiffre du sondeur sur la connexion QUIC vers le relais, si le relais répond à la sonde (`lossScope = 2`) ». §16.1 allows 2 connections per peer, so two connections to the relay can coexist.
kept.evidence: internal/transport/p2p/links.go:268-288 relayConn: its doc says « returns our connection to the relay that carries the circuit », but it returns « rcs[0] » of ConnsToPeer(relay) with no check of transport or circuit. links.go:223-228: « if rc := n.relayConn(...); rc != nil { if _, ok := quicStats(rc); ok { c, s.scope = rc, transport.LossFirstHop } } ».
kept.scenario: The node holds a TCP and a QUIC connection to its relay, and ConnsToPeer lists the TCP one first. quicStats(rc) fails, so the relayed link shows lossPermille 0xFFFF and lossScope 0, even though the probe runs and has a figure on the QUIC connection to the same relay. The opposite case gives the figure of a connection that does not carry the circuit. Display only: §8.5.5 forbids decisions on the figure, and probe_arch_test.go enforces that.
kept.fix: In relayConn, prefer a raw QUIC connection to the relay whose probe exists (n.probes.of(c.ID()) != nil), and fix the doc comment. Or state in Annex A.1 which connection is meant when there are several.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. relayConn (links.go:268-288) is documented as returning 'our connection to the relay that carries the circuit', but it returns rcs[0] of ConnsToPeer(relay) without checking which connection carries the circuit or what its transport is. probeLink (links.go:223-228) then sets LossFirstHop only if quicStats(rc) succeeds. Nodes and relays enable both QUIC and TCP (node.go:384-389, relay.go:125-130), so a TCP connection and a QUIC connection to the same relay can coexist. If the TCP one is listed first, the first-hop figure shows as unknown even though a QUIC probe is running, and with two QUIC connections the figure can come from one that does not carry the circuit. The figure is only displayed (§8.5.5), so this stays minor.

Confirmed. links.go:268-288: relayConn finds the circuit's relay and returns `rcs[0]` of ConnsToPeer(relay), with no preference for a QUIC connection. links.go:223-228 then needs quicStats(rc) to succeed. The node runs both QUIC and TCP transports (node.go:385, :389), so two connections to the relay can coexist. When the TCP one comes first, the relayed link shows an unknown figure, although Annex A.1 asks for the prober's figure on the QUIC connection to the relay. The doc comment (`the relay that carries the circuit`) is also not checked. Display only (§8.5.5 forbids decisions on the figure), and it needs the less common two-connection state, so minor.

kept.title: Documentation drift in the reference: the PTO doc says 25 ms (spec and constant: 26 ms); the ADR counts 147 vectors (149)
kept.question: proof
kept.rule: §8.5.5 step 3.6: « max_ack_delay … ou 26 ms si l'implémentation QUIC ne l'expose pas »; §16.1: « `max_ack_delay` 26 ms s'il n'est pas exposé ». README point 8: the vectors are the public reference.
kept.evidence: protocol/linkprobe/machines.go:49-51: « maxAckDelay < 0 means the QUIC stack does not expose the peer's: 25 ms is used », while the code uses transport.LinkProbeDefaultMaxAckDelay, protocol/limits.go:336 « = 26 * time.Millisecond ». docs/adr/0036-link-probe.md:340: « (147 vectors: …) », while protocol/vectors/linkprobe.json has 149 vector ids.
kept.scenario: A third party implementing from the godoc of the reference package uses 25 ms. Its PTO is 1 ms shorter than the spec's, so an echo that arrives exactly at the bound is marked Late where the vectors say accepted, and linkprobe-pto-no-max-ack-delay fails for a reason the doc hides.

The PTO doc in machines.go:49-51 says '25 ms is used', while the code uses transport.LinkProbeDefaultMaxAckDelay = 26 * time.Millisecond (protocol/limits.go:336), as the spec requires.
