dropped.title: Reference Host accepts a negotiation that succeeds 10 s or more after the open, unless a Tick ran in between

verdicts.reason: The cited lines are correct: host.go:163 checks the 10 s deadline only in Tick, and Negotiated (host.go:204-222) never compares now-h.negoSince. But inkwell's I/O layer already blocks the scenario. probe.go:323 wraps the negotiation in context.WithTimeout(pc.ctx, wire.LinkProbeNegotiationTimeout), and probe.go:341-345 resets the stream and turns a late success into ctx.Err(). A confirmation at 10.5 s therefore never reaches Host.Negotiated(ok=true). The auditor agrees nothing is reachable in inkwell. The only remaining case is a hypothetical third-party I/O layer, so the finding is refuted. At most it is a doc note on Host saying that the I/O layer owns the deadline.

Confirmed in the public reference. protocol/linkprobe/host.go:163 checks the 10 s only in Tick (`h.negotiating && now-h.negoSince >= transport.LinkProbeNegotiationTimeout`). Negotiated (host.go:204-222) sets `h.negotiating = false` and goes on to Open/probeNow without looking at now-negoSince. Spec §8.5.3 (spec.md:1215-1217) says a negotiation that has not succeeded 10 s after the open is reset, and §8.5.5 step 2 (spec.md:1322-1324) makes the end of the negotiation a trigger, so the rule applies at Negotiated(10500). The only vector, linkprobe-host-negotiation-timeout (linkprobe.json:6209-6238), drives ticks at 9999 and 10000 and never a late Negotiated. inkwell itself cannot reach it: probe.go:323 and :341-345 put a 10 s context and AfterFunc reset on the negotiation. So the defect is in the reusable reference Host (README point 8), not in the app. Minor.

dropped.title: An identifier for a 1.x minor is not specified: a peer that advertises /inkwell/linkprobe/1.1.0 would get na and never be probed

verdicts.reason: The spec does say what the identifier carries. §1.4.2 (spec.md:62) says multistream-select negotiates the protocol identifier per major ('identifiant de protocole (majeure)'). §8.5.9 (spec.md:1547-1548) says the prober 'propose ses majeures … aujourd'hui seulement 1.0.0'. A minor only adds ignorable types (spec.md:1549-1551, §20.8 at :2256-2260), and a 1.0 reader skips those, so a minor needs no new identifier. Proposing /inkwell/linkprobe/1.1.0 goes against 'propose ses majeures'. The '1.x' in the §20.8 title names a family of versions, not a wire identifier. There is no code defect: message.go ProtocolID and probe.go:62 match the spec.

The spec is not ambiguous here. §1.4.2 (spec.md:62) says the protocol identifier carries the major (`identifiant de protocole (majeure)`). §8.5.9 (spec.md:1547-1548) says the prober proposes its majors (`propose ses majeures … aujourd'hui seulement 1.0.0`). §20.6 (spec.md:2244-2250) applies the same rule to every identifier: minors add things without changing the identifier (`une nouvelle classe de session s'ajoute par une mineure, liée à une capacité`). §20.8's `/1.x` title names the registry of the 1 major, not a wire string. A third party proposing `/inkwell/linkprobe/1.1.0` is not conformant. The spec does not leave this to guess.

dropped.title: GREASE DEVRAIT of §8.5.9 not implemented: no inkwell endpoint ever sends an ignorable on the probe streams

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. In the probe code, the only writes are Encode of a PROBE (host.go:192) and of an ECHO (host.go:321), and probe.go only forwards WriteOut/WriteIn. A grep over the non-test Go sources finds GREASE only in protocol/cmd/vectors, so no emitter exists. The spec's own proof table (spec.md:1634) admits 'la référence n'en écrit pas'. That leaves the DEVRAIT of §8.5.9 (spec.md:1558-1561) unmet, and the only proof of the skip path is reader-side vectors. It is a SHOULD with no security impact, hence minor. The gap also seems to exist beyond P7: no GREASE emitter turned up for CONTROL either.

Already known and documented. The spec's own proof table (spec.md:1634) records for `GREASE de l'émetteur` that `par construction : la référence n'en écrit pas`. The obligation is a DEVRAIT (SHOULD, spec.md:1558), not a DOIT. The reader-side rule that GREASE protects is proven by the linkprobe-prober-ignorable-*, linkprobe-responder-ignorable-* and linkprobe-host-inbound-ignorables vectors (spec.md:1633). This is a deliberate, recorded choice, not an unknown defect.

dropped.title: I/O layer resets every probe stream after its clean close, which the spec does not describe

verdicts.reason: The code does what is cited. readOut resets after any read error, EOF included (probe.go:401-410). serve's defer waits up to 10 s for in.w.end and then calls s.Reset() (probe.go:426-439). In quic-go v0.64.1, CancelWrite (send_stream.go:648-685) still queues a RESET_STREAM after Close. But the spec makes this harmless. A closing prober 'lit et jette … jusqu'à la fin du côté du répondeur' (spec.md:1245-1249), and any end counts as that end. The spec also says any reset is handled the same way and the peer MUST NOT interpret the code (spec.md:1253-1255). host.go:227-230 treats both endings alike, and the FIN has already been handed to the transport before the reset. No peer-visible state differs, and a third party that counts a reset as abnormal could only count it, since violations change nothing (spec.md:1326-1327). This is wire hygiene, not a reachable defect.

The spec allows it. spec.md:1240 says a stream ends by a FIN read or by a reset from either side. spec.md:1253-1255 says a reset is a Reset with code 0 and `le pair NE DOIT PAS interpréter le code : toute réinitialisation se traite de la même façon`. Nothing forbids a reset after the FIN exchange, and a closing prober must accept any end of the responder's side (host.go:227-230: OutboundEnded handles a FIN or a reset alike, and the closing branch only clears state). The `strict third-party prober` that counts a reset as abnormal would itself break the spec. Also, by the time the prober's readOut sees EOF (probe.go:401-410), the responder has already read the prober's FIN. So the reset has no effect on either state machine.

kept.title: An unattested stranger can make Go hold about 40 000 unverified attestations per identity during an invitation window, with no total
kept.question: hostile-peer
kept.rule: §5.1 (spec.md:591-592): a non-member let in by the invitation window may open only /inkwell/lobby/1.0.0, any other stream is reset; §5.3 (:629-630) nothing else is accepted before HELLO; §16.1 (:2100) attestations awaiting their signer: 2 periods, in the share of the delivering peer; threat model: unattested peers strictly bounded. Inventaire N-13 (inventaire.md:76) rated this « Mineur » for members only.
kept.evidence: internal/transport/p2p/node.go:538 `return n.opts.Admit == nil || n.opts.Admit(name) || n.isOpen()`; stream.go:47 `admitted := n.admitted(p)` then :58 startOpenLocked opens our sync stream, and :234 handleStream accepts the stranger's /inkwell/sync/1.0.0 stream; internal/app/wiring.go:417 `w.up[ev.Peer] = struct{}{}` on any PeerUp; attest.go:235-237 `if _, connected := w.up[ev.Peer]; connected { if a, err := trust.DecodeAttestation(ev.Payload); err == nil { w.hold(ev.Peer, a) } }` (no signature, role or project check); attest.go:290 `const maxHeld = 4 * maxPending` = 40 000 (internal/project/tree.go:24 MaxNodes = 10000); attest.go:297-308 hold keys by (Doc, Signer), Doc chosen freely (protocol/trust/attest.go:49 Doc ≤ 256 bytes); kept until PeerDown (wiring.go:421), no time limit; node.go:91 maxPeers = 64 inbound connections; window opened by internal/app/invites.go:183.
kept.scenario: An admin opens an invitation (SetOpen). An attacker on the LAN (mDNS) or holding the address connects with a fresh key, gets PeerUp, and streams 40 000 well-formed attestations with distinct Doc strings (≈2.4 KiB each decoded: 256-byte doc + 64 heads). Go keeps ≈96 MiB for that identity; repeating with 64 identities fills ≈6 GiB of Go heap before the window closes, without ever being a member or signing anything valid.
kept.fix: Enforce §5.1: handleStream and startOpenLocked must use Options.Admit only (window-only peers get the lobby, nothing else). Restrict hold to the single peer named by the join in flight (the host of the redeemed ticket), cap it globally, and expire held entries after 2 periods as §16.1 says; verify signature and project before keeping.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed and reachable. node.go:538 admits any valid peer while the window is open; stream.go:47-58 marks it admitted and opens our stream, and handleStream (:234-275) pushes its frames once it is up. wiring.go:416-417 adds every PeerUp to w.up, and reconcile (:487-505) only walks members, so a stranger is never dropped. attest.go:232-237 holds any attestation that decodes for a peer in w.up, with no signature, project or role check. hold (:297-308) caps one peer at maxHeld = 4*maxPending = 40 000 keys, with no total across peers, and keeps them until PeerDown (wiring.go:421). This breaks §12 step 1 (spec.md:1987: a stranger in the window may reach the lobby only). Lowered to major: it needs an open window (joinWindow is 2 min, invites.go:24; the host window is set by invites.go:183) and a network position, and the cost is about 96 MiB per identity times 64 connections (node.go:91). Not new either: docs/protocol/inventaire.md:76 (N-13) already records '40 000 par pair, sans total (64 pairs × 40 000 × 4 Kio)' for any peer that is not active yet, not for members only as the finding says.

Confirmed. node.go:529-539 admitted() is true for any valid peer while isOpen(); stream.go:47-58 then opens our sync stream (so PeerUp is sent) and stream.go:234 handleStream accepts the stranger's sync stream with only the same admitted() check, so a window guest is not limited to the lobby. wiring.go:417 puts every PeerUp in w.up; attest.go:235-237 holds any attestation that decodes, with no signature, role or project check; attest.go:290 maxHeld = 4*project.MaxNodes = 40 000 per peer (tree.go:24); hold (:297-308) keys by (Doc, Signer) and checks only the per-peer count; the entry is removed only at PeerDown (wiring.go:421). That makes about 100 MB per identity, with up to 64 inbound connections (node.go:91, :489). This is inventaire N-13 (inventaire.md:76), which is not on the brief's list of known findings, and its 'Mineur' rating ignores strangers. kept.title: Kept attestations have no global or per-signer bound: one Byzantine writer exhausts the memory of every member
kept.question: hostile-peer
kept.rule: §16.1 kept attestations row (spec.md:2099): per (doc, signer) ≤ 256 distinct heads, 65 536 keys and 64 MiB in total, share ⌊C / standing signers⌋; §10.6 reserved shares; §17 « Épuisement » (:2147): every map has a bound and an owner. Inventaire S3 (inventaire.md:52) is still open.
kept.evidence: internal/app/attest.go:36 `latest map[attestKey]trust.Attestation` with no size check in add (:42-51); offerAttest (:256-274) stores any attestation that passes List.Verify, which checks project, signature and writer role only (protocol/trust/attest.go:134-155), Doc is any UTF-8 of 1-256 bytes (:49), never tied to the admitted set; every new key is relayed to all active peers (:267) and notified to the webview; sendAttestations (:276-280) replays the whole map to each newly active peer. Constants protocol.AttestationKeys / AttestationBytes / AttestationDistinctHeads (protocol/limits.go:191-196) are referenced by no code. The webview bounds the same object (coverage: 1024 docs per signer, 10 000 docs, §16.2) while Go does not: Go and TypeScript disagree on the bound.
kept.scenario: A member with the writer role signs attestations for doc = "a0", "a1", … (all valid, one per key). kept.fix: Implement the §6.2/§10.6 store: per (doc, signer) a set capped at 256 distinct heads with eviction by smallest seq; a global cap (65 536 keys, 64 MiB) split in per-signer shares; refuse or do not relay attestations for documents outside the admitted set; one table of constants from protocol/limits.go with bound, bound+1 and recovery tests.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. attestStore.add (attest.go:42-51) has no size check. offerAttest (:256-274) stores anything that passes List.Verify, which checks only project, signature, writer role and suspension (protocol/trust/attest.go:134-155), and relays it to every active peer. Confirmed. attest.go:36-51 attestStore.add has no size check. offerAttest (:256-274) stores whatever passes List.Verify, which checks only project, field form, signature and writer standing (protocol/trust/attest.go:133-155): Doc is any 1-256 byte UTF-8 string, never tied to the admitted set. Every new key is relayed to all active peers (:267-271), and sendAttestations (:276-280) replays the whole map to each new peer. protocol.AttestationKeys/AttestationBytes/AttestationDistinctHeads (limits.go:191-196) are referenced nowhere else (grep). criticKept.title: One admitted peer freezes every peer's sync and file reception by announcing a large frame and then sending nothing: the shared receive budget is reserved on the announced length and nothing ever times out
criticKept.question: hostile-peer
criticKept.rule: §10.1 (spec.md:1826-1829): « Une boucle partagée par plusieurs pairs NE DOIT jamais attendre un pair. Un dépassement ne coûte qu'à celui qui l'a causé. Tout plafond partagé a des parts réservées ». §10.2 (spec.md:1845-1848): only « l'arrêt complet » of a transfer the receiver has reserved triggers a failure, so a reservation that stops progressing has to fail. §10.6 (spec.md:1885-1894): memory reserved ahead of time gets a fixed share r = C / N_max, so « un principal qui retient de la capacité (lecture au compte-gouttes) ne retient que la sienne ». §16.1: the REPO input queue is per peer, 4 MiB (spec.md:2069); a LARGE stream with no byte for 60 s while reserved is reset (spec.md:2087). Threat model: readers and unattested peers are strictly bounded.
criticKept.evidence: internal/transport/frame/frame.go:77-86: ReadReserve calls reserve(n) with the announced size « before anything is allocated », before any payload byte arrives. internal/transport/p2p/stream.go:259-268: handleStream passes cost = min(size+msgOverhead, maxBuffered) to n.budget.Acquire(cost). That is a blocking wait (frame/budget.go:23-34) on one budget shared by every peer: maxBuffered = 256 << 20 (node.go:118-119), msgOverhead = 64 (node.go:117). No read deadline is set on the sync stream: the only SetReadDeadline in p2p is in lobby.go:69. MaxFrame = 64<<20 - 3 - 64 (protocol/peer.go:7,29), so one claim costs 64 MiB - 3. Up to 4 sync streams per peer are allowed (node.go:92, 493-497). A peer's extra streams wait for the previous one for at most reorderWait = 1 min and then read anyway (stream.go:251-258; node.go:114). The bulk lane is worse: its whole budget is one frame, bulkBuffered = transport.MaxFrame + msgOverhead (bulk.go:27-29, 61), reserved the same way with no deadline (bulk.go:162-171). The only admission check is n.admitted(p), with no role check (stream.go:234; bulk.go:140). The mux reassembly draws on the same budget through Node.Reserve = TryAcquire (node.go:807; mux/fragment.go:342-347). When that fails it evicts the other peers' partial messages and then its own (fragment.go:330-333, 274-276). frame.go:23-26 says « a peer that only claims a large length costs little memory ». The only test of this, TestReadDoesNotPreallocate (frame_extra_test.go:197-208), measures allocation and not the budget. WriteBudget.tla:22-26 and SendPath.tla model one sender facing one hostile reader; the receive budget under a hostile sender is modelled nowhere.
criticKept.scenario: Bulk lane: a reader member opens /inkwell/bulk/1.0.0 and writes the 4-byte header 0x03FFFFBD (= MaxFrame), then nothing, keeping the connection alive. The connection is protected after PeerUp (stream.go:116). b.budget.Acquire takes the entire bulk budget. From then on every other peer's handleBulk loop blocks in Acquire, and no file transfer is received from anyone until the reader disconnects, possibly never. Sync lane: the same reader opens its 4 sync streams one minute apart and sends the same header on each. They hold 4 × (64 MiB - 3) = 256 MiB - 12 bytes. Every honest frame (cost ≥ 65) then blocks in Acquire, and every fragmented message fails its TryAcquire and is dropped silently (R-Evict). Document sync, the member list and attestations stop for every peer. Two colluding identities, or Sybil strangers during an invitation window (P6 kept finding: strangers reach the sync and bulk streams), do it at once. The attack costs a few bytes and goes unnoticed: no fault, no log, no timeout.
criticKept.fix: Give the receive budgets per-peer shares, as §10.6 requires. A peer may reserve at most a fixed share: the 4 MiB REPO input queue of §16.1 for sync, and a per-peer slot for bulk. Reservations that would exceed the share use TryAcquire on the free part only, never a blocking Acquire on the shared total. Charge a frame as its bytes arrive, or arm a progress deadline once the header is read (the 60 s without a byte of §16.1 l.2087). Reset the stream and count a fault when it expires. Add a test with two peers where one sends only a MaxFrame header and the other's frames must still be delivered. Model the receive side with a hostile sender (extend WriteBudget or SendPath with N senders over one budget). Related to inventaire N-5 (flooding), but the trigger is different: no data has to be sent, and no deadline exists on the read side.
criticKept.block: ADR 0034 step 5 (N-5, shared non-blocking loops and per-peer shares); interim fix on sync/1 before step 6
